key_insight: Cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsation temporarily suppresses turbulence, while delayed turbulent shear recovery sustains a low-drag interval before momentum transport rebounds.
engineering_relevance: Understanding phase-dependent turbulence recovery could guide pulsatile pipe-flow control strategies that target drag reduction.
method: Direct numerical simulations of cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow.
Four cases spanning two Reynolds-number ranges, with and without a low-flow plateau.
Phase-resolved turbulence analysis and unsteady friction decomposition.
evidence_signal: Across the simulated cases, streamwise-stress production recovers before redistribution and radial transport, while a low-flow plateau prolongs turbulence decay and delays local instability.
watch_item: The abstract reports four simulation cases but no experimental validation, so transfer to broader operating conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics in cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow
